page.layout: One page of text, with a running head and page number at the top right. Below the text: the closing words "FINIS HISTORIARVM" and "THEOPHYLACTI" in capitals, then a woodcut ornament. A catchword sits at the lower right. Left-edge fragments belong to the neighbouring page and are not transcribed.

main_text.p: constaret, Legatos ad Mauricium misit de captiuis recipiendis: Erant ea millia septemdecim cum du-ducentis: Mauricius itaque minis barbari percuf-fus, orationeque circumuentus, per tabellarium Prisco mandauit, ut captiuos redderet Chagano Abaros. accita quidem a periculo liberi redduntur Chagano bar-bari.

page.notes: The woodcut ornament below the closing words is not transcribed as text. The first line of the page ("constaret") starts mid-sentence and is a fragment carried over from the previous page. The line "Erant ea millia septemdecim cum du-" is followed by "ducentis" on the next line; the printed reading there is partly unclear ("ducentis.:" with a stray mark), so the hyphenation is marked as read. The running head and the "THEO." catchword are read from a low-contrast scan and should be checked.
